Day Master page · card 4 · dev build · 庚 The Blade

Card 4, four ways to set the pictures

The same five paintings and texts on the real card, laid out four ways, each aiming to make the text part of the painting rather than a caption beneath it. All four are live on the dev build behind a switch.

Reply with one code, for example "B", or a code plus changes. My pick is B: the round fan is the most traditional thumbnail form, it lets the reading wrap the painting, and it gives the most compact card (about a quarter shorter than the locked band).

Locked pass

Band under the title

The painting is a shallow band between the name and the three words. Clean, but the picture and the text sit in separate layers, one after the other.

A

Painted heading

The painting becomes the row's heading and the title is written into its empty paper on the left, like an inscription on a painting. The chips tuck under its fading foot. Strongest picture, longest card.

B

Round fan leaf (团扇)

Recommended

The painting is cropped into a round fan leaf, the classic small-format painting, and replaces the ink dot as the row's thumbnail. The element sign sits on its rim like a seal, and the words and reading wrap around the circle. Most organic, and the most compact card.

C

Text wraps the picture

A square crop floats on alternating sides and the reading flows around it, like a picture book. Lively rhythm, but the ragged text edge is harder to read on a phone.
